'''Raphaël Xavier Varane''' ({{IPA|fr|ʁafaɛl vaʁan|lang}}; born 25 April 1993) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[centre-back]]. Often called the term "[[Rolls-Royce car|Rolls-Royce]]" defender in football, he is regarded as one of the best defenders of his generation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-28|title=Manchester United: Raphael Varane is a 'Rolls-Royce' signing|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cj7g4gpnnveo|access-date=2026-07-07|website=BBC Sport|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Anka|first=Carl|date=2021-09-25|title=The Raphael Varane documentary and why defenders like to be compared to (certain) cars|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2814283/2021/09/24/the-raphael-varane-documentary-and-why-defenders-like-to-be-compared-to-certain-cars/|access-date=2026-07-10|work=The New York Times|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lines |first=Breaking The |date=2021-07-29 |title=Player Analysis: Raphaël Varane |url=https://breakingthelines.com/@btl/player-analysis-raphael-varane |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=Breaking The Lines |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=OneFootball·2 min |date=2024-09-25 |title='Too many games' - Why Raphaël Varane has been forced to retire at 31 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/too-many-games-why-rapha-130400111.html |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2021-07-29 |title='Complete centre-back' Varane was world’s ‘best defender’ at 18 and is like Rio |url=https://talksport.com/football/918016/raphael-varane-age-man-utd-stats-eden-hazard-jose-mourinho/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-gb}}</ref> 

Varane played for French club [[RC Lens|Lens]] at youth level and, ahead of the [[2010–11 in French football|2010–11 season]], began training with the senior team and appeared on the bench in several league matches. Varane made his professional debut in 2010 aged 17,<ref name="varane_debut">{{cite web |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53778 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Lens v. Montpellier Match Report |language=fr |date=6 November 2010 |access-date=6 November 2010}}</ref> and after one season as a professional footballer, he joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. There, over the course of ten seasons from 2011 to 2021, he won eighteen trophies, including three [[La Liga]] titles, one [[Copa del Rey]], four [[UEFA Champions League]] titles and four [[FIFA Club World Cup]]s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/football/squad/raphael-varane# |title=Raphaël Varane |publisher= Real Madrid CF}}</ref> In 2021, Varane left Real Madrid to sign for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], where he won the [[2022–23 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2023–24 FA Cup|FA Cup]] during a three-year spell. He departed England in 2024, joining newly-promoted [[Serie A]] side [[Como 1907|Como]] as a free agent, but after playing just 23 minutes for the club, picked up a knee injury and was removed from the squad list, before subsequently announcing his retirement from professional football in September 2024. After retiring from playing football, he joined the board of education working with youth players for Como 1907.

Varane represented France at [[France national under-18 football team|under-18]], [[France national under-20 football team|under-20]] and [[France national under-21 football team|under-21]] level, before making his [[France national football team|senior international]] debut in March 2013. He was part of France's [[FIFA World Cup]] squad in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]], when he was nominated for the [[FIFA World Cup awards#FIFA Young Player Award|Best Young Player]] award,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=7/news=depay-pogba-and-varane-make-up-best-young-player-shortlist-2403365.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140711210817/http://www.fifa.com//worldcup/news/y=2014/m=7/news=depay-pogba-and-varane-make-up-best-young-player-shortlist-2403365.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 July 2014 |title=2018 FIFA World Cup Russia - News - Depay, Pogba and Varane make up Hyundai Young Player Award shortlist |website=FIFA.com}}</ref> in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]], when he played every minute as France went on to win the competition, and in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]], when France finished as runners-up. He additionally appeared at [[UEFA Euro 2020]], and was part of the France squad that won the [[UEFA Nations League]] in [[2021 UEFA Nations League Finals|2021]]. Varane announced his retirement from international football in 2023, having earned 93 caps and scored five goals.

==Early life==
Raphaël Xavier Varane<ref>{{cite web |url=http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpActa1?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=23166 |title=Acta del Partido celebrado el 26 de marzo de 2014, en Sevilla |trans-title=Minutes of the Match held on 26 March 2014, in Seville |publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117210911/http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpActa1?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=23166 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |language=es}}</ref> was born on 25 April 1993<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifadata.com/documents/FWC/2018/pdf/FWC_2018_SQUADLISTS.PDF |title=FIFA World Cup Russia 2018: List of Players: France |publisher=FIFA |page=11 |date=15 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190611000407/https://www.fifadata.com/documents/FWC/2018/pdf/FWC_2018_SQUADLISTS.PDF |archive-date=11 June 2019}}</ref> in the city of [[Lille]] in the Nord department.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/fiche/raphael-varane/215142 |title=Raphaël Varane |newspaper=L'Équipe |location=Paris |access-date=6 June 2026 |language=fr}}</ref> He is of [[Demographics of Martinique|Martiniquais]] heritage through his father, Gaston, who is originally from [[Le Morne-Rouge]], while his mother, Annie, was raised in [[Saint-Amand-les-Eaux]].<ref name="varane_antilles">{{cite web |url=http://www.antilles-foot.com/2011/01/29/raphael-varane-volontaire-et-determine/ |publisher=Antilles-foot |title=Raphael Varane: Volontaire et déterminé. |language=fr |date=29 January 2011 |access-date=23 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20110912131656/http://www.antilles-foot.com/2011/01/29/raphael-varane-volontaire-et-determine/ |archive-date=12 September 2011}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Varane began his football career in the [[Arrondissement of Lille]] playing for local club Hellemmes at the age of seven.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nordeclair.fr/Locales/Lille/2010/05/03/l-ash-en-tournoi-international.shtml |publisher=Nord Eclair |title=L'ASH en tournoi international |language=fr |date=3 May 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011 |archive-date=27 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727113247/http://www.nordeclair.fr/Locales/Lille/2010/05/03/l-ash-en-tournoi-international.shtml |url-status=dead}}</ref> After spending two years at the club, in July 2002, he joined professional club [[RC Lens|Lens]], despite some interest from [[Derby du Nord]] rivals and hometown club [[Lille OSC|Lille]].<ref name="varane_career">{{cite web |url=http://www.lensois.com/article-1910-varane-j-ai-grandi-au-rc-lens-.html |publisher=Lensois |title=Varane: "J'ai grandi au RC Lens" |language=fr |date=10 March 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100819091137/http://www.lensois.com/article-1910-varane-j-ai-grandi-au-rc-lens-.html |archive-date=19 August 2010}}</ref> Similar to the development of the club's previous prized assets such as [[Gaël Kakuta]] and [[Timothée Kolodziejczak]], Varane spent time at the Centre de Préformation de Football in nearby [[Liévin]], a training centre exclusively for players brought up in the Nord-Pas-de-Calais region.<ref name="varane_antilles"/> He spent two years at the centre training there during the weekdays and playing with Lens on the weekends.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

After returning full-time to Lens, Varane quickly ascended up the club's youth ranks. In the 2008–09 season, alongside teammates [[Thorgan Hazard]] and [[Geoffrey Kondogbia]], he played on the club's under-16 team that won the ''Championnat National des 16 ans''. In the following season, Varane was promoted to the club's under-19 team, despite being two years younger than several of his teammates. Ahead of the [[2010–11 in French football|2010–11 season]], Varane signed his first professional contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rclensois.fr/contrats/varane-et-deligny-egalement-pros-a7655.html |publisher=RC Lensois |title=Varane et Deligny également pros? |language=fr |date=16 April 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref> He was, subsequently, promoted to the club's reserve team in the [[Championnat de France amateur]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lensois.com/breve-34965-Ab%C3%A9c%C3%A9daire%3A%20V%20comme%20Rapha%C3%ABl%20Varane.html |publisher=Lensois |title=Abécédaire: V comme Raphaël Varane |language=fr |date=1 January 2011 |access-date=14 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110105062246/http://www.lensois.com/breve-34965-Ab%C3%A9c%C3%A9daire:%20V%20comme%20Rapha%C3%ABl%20Varane.html |archive-date=5 January 2011}}</ref> Varane made his amateur debut in the club's opening league match of the campaign in a 2–0 victory over [[JA Drancy|Drancy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.foot-national.com/fiche-match-football-19483.html |publisher=Foot-National |title=Lens v. Drancy Match Report |language=fr |date=1 January 2011 |access-date=14 January 2011 |archive-date=18 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200718142022/http://www.foot-national.com/match-foot-lens-drancy-19483.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He appeared as a starter in the club's next nine matches with the team losing only one of them.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

===Lens===
In late October of the campaign, Varane was called up to the senior team by manager [[Jean-Guy Wallemme]] to train ahead of the club's match against [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] on 6 November. He trained with the team for the entire week and, due to an injury to [[centre-back]] [[Alaeddine Yahia]], Varane was, surprisingly, named to the starting line-up.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lavoixdessports.com/L-info-Sports-en-continu/Region/2010/11/06/article_football-rc-lens-raphael-varane-devrait-debuter.shtml |publisher=La Voix des Sports |title=Raphaël Varane débutera face à Montpellier dimanche |language=fr |date=6 November 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref> In the match, he played the full 90 minutes in a 2–0 victory.<ref name="varane_debut"/> The victory was only the club's third [[clean sheet]] of the season. Varane was praised by teammates, most notably [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Adil Hermach]], defensive partner [[Éric Chelle]], and [[Striker (association football)|striker]] [[David Pollet]], as well as by the local media and coach Wallemme.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nordeclair.fr/Sports/Football/2010/11/09/lens-emporte-par-le-souffle-de-la-jeunes.shtml |publisher=Nord Eclair |title=Lens emporté par le souffle de la jeunesse |language=fr |date=9 November 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011 |archive-date=27 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727113308/http://www.nordeclair.fr/Sports/Football/2010/11/09/lens-emporte-par-le-souffle-de-la-jeunes.shtml |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lensois.com/breve-rclens-33699--j-ai-ete-surpris-par-rapha%C3%ABl-varane-.html |publisher=Lensois |title=J'ai été surpris par Raphaël Varane |language=fr |date=19 November 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101231043704/http://www.lensois.com/breve-rclens-33699--j-ai-ete-surpris-par-rapha%C3%ABl-varane-.html |archive-date=31 December 2010}}</ref> In the next two matches, Varane, alongside several other youth players, sat on the bench as Lens faced two tough teams in [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] and [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53751 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Marseille v. Lens Match Report |language=fr |date=13 November 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53756 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Lens v. Lyon Match Report |language=fr |date=21 November 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref> He returned to the starting line-up on 30 November in a 4–1 defeat to [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/73810 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Brest v. Lens Match Report |language=fr |date=30 November 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref> Despite the firing of Wallemme following the Brest match, Varane remained a starter in the team under new manager [[László Bölöni]]. In December, with both Chelle and Yahia returning to action, Varane was placed in the defensive midfielder role in the team's match against [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]]. In the match, he acted as a roving third centre-back and made a blocked save in the 84th minute on a close range shot by [[Yoan Gouffran]] to preserve a 2–1 lead.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/match_commentary/0,19764,11065_3280760,00.html |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |title=Match Commentary: Bordeaux v. Lens |date=22 December 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref> However, in the latter stages of the match, Bordeaux equalized to draw the match at 2–2.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53803 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Bordeaux v. Lens Match Report |language=fr |date=22 December 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref>

In early 2011, Varane was the subject of transfer speculation linking him to several clubs.<ref>{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |title=Manchester United poised to sign Lens prospect Raphaël Varane |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/may/18/manchester-united-raphael-varane-lens |access-date=1 September 2020 |work=The Guardian |date=18 May 2011}}</ref> In an effort to quell the interest, on 3 February 2011, he signed a two-year contract extension with Lens until 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lensois.com/article-2747-varane-j-ai-prolonge-a-lens-jusqu-en-2015-.html |publisher=Lensois |title=Varane: "J'ai prolongé à Lens jusqu'en 2015" |language=fr |date=3 February 2011 |access-date=5 February 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110205121105/http://www.lensois.com/article-2747-varane-j-ai-prolonge-a-lens-jusqu-en-2015-.html |archive-date=5 February 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lavoixdunord.fr/Region/Breves/Breves_Sports/2011/02/04/article_football-lens-raphael-varane-prolonge-jusqu-en.shtml |publisher=La Voix du Nord |title=Raphaël Varane prolonge jusqu'en 2015 |language=fr |date=4 February 2011 |access-date=5 February 2011 |archive-date=27 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927132347/http://www.lavoixdunord.fr/Region/Breves/Breves_Sports/2011/02/04/article_football-lens-raphael-varane-prolonge-jusqu-en.shtml |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chronofoot.com/lens/raphael-varane-prolonge-a-lens_mrm133464.html |publisher=Chronofoot |title=Raphael Varane prolonge à Lens! |language=fr |date=3 February 2011 |access-date=5 February 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121208193244/http://www.chronofoot.com/lens/raphael-varane-prolonge-a-lens_mrm133464.html |archive-date=8 December 2012}}</ref> On 8 May, Varane scored his first professional goal in a 1–1 draw with [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53985 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Caen v. Lens Match Report |language=fr |date=7 May 2011 |access-date=7 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110510145006/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53985 |archive-date=10 May 2011}}</ref> In the team's following match against [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], he scored the equalizing goal in another 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53989 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Monaco v. Lens Match Report |language=fr |date=15 May 2011 |access-date=18 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110518133718/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53989 |archive-date=18 May 2011}}</ref> Despite the goal, the stalemate condemned Lens to relegation back to Ligue 2 after two seasons in the top division.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/920251/ligue-1:-lens-relegated-after-monaco-stalemate |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110519205402/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/920251/ligue-1:-lens-relegated-after-monaco-stalemate |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 May 2011 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |title=Lens go down after Monaco draw |date=15 May 2011 |access-date=18 May 2011}}</ref> On 21 May, Varane captained Lens in its 1–0 defeat to [[AC Arles-Avignon|Arles-Avignon]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53994 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |title=Lens v. Arles-Avignon Match Report |language=fr |date=21 May 2011 |access-date=21 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110524141443/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/53994 |archive-date=24 May 2011}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
====2011–12: Signing and La Liga win====
[[File:Raphaël Varane in Real Madrid.jpg|thumb|upright|Varane training with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2011]]

On 22 June 2011, Lens president [[Gervais Martel]] confirmed to a group of supporters at a club meeting that Varane would be joining [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref name="varane_madrid">{{cite web |url=http://www.rclens.fr/infos_2011/06/22_reunion_supporters/index.php |publisher=[[RC Lens]] |title=Gervais Martel a répondu aux supporters |language=fr |date=22 June 2011 |access-date=22 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623142804/http://www.rclens.fr/infos_2011/06/22_reunion_supporters/index.php#ancreContenu |archive-date=23 June 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/breves2011/20110622_233831_varane-au-real-selon-martel.html |publisher=[[L'Equipe]] |title=Varane au Real selon Martel |language=fr |date=22 June 2011 |access-date=22 June 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110625032210/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/breves2011/20110622_233831_varane-au-real-selon-martel.html |archive-date=25 June 2011}}</ref> Varane had previously visited Real Madrid's club facilities and also met with club advisor and compatriot [[Zinedine Zidane]].<ref name="varane_madrid"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/930702/real-madrid-confirm-capture-of-lens-starlet-raphael-varane?cc=5739 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110703112347/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/930702/real-madrid-confirm-capture-of-lens-starlet-raphael-varane?cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 July 2011 |title=Real confirm capture of starlet Varane |date=27 June 2011 |publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=27 June 2011}}</ref> On 27 June, the move was confirmed by Real Madrid after Varane passed his medical. Varane signed a six-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330061731207/noticia/Noticia/Raphael_Varane_firma_su_contrato_con_el_Real_Madrid.htm |title=Raphaël Varane firma su contrato con el Real Madrid |date=27 June 2011 |work=[[Real Madrid CF]]|access-date=27 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110630144003/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330061731207/noticia/Noticia/Raphael_Varane_firma_su_contrato_con_el_Real_Madrid.htm |archive-date=30 June 2011}}</ref>

Varane was assigned the number 19 shirt and made his club debut for Real Madrid in the club's opening pre-season fixture against American outfit [[LA Galaxy|Los Angeles Galaxy]] in the [[2011 World Football Challenge]]. He appeared as a half-time substitute as Real Madrid cruised to a 4–1 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/real-madrid-boss-mourinho-delighted-debut-boys-la-galaxy-win-1763141 |title=Real Madrid boss Mourinho delighted with debut boys in LA Galaxy win |date=16 July 2011 |work=tribalfootball.com}}</ref> Varane made his first start for the club four days later in a 3–0 win over Mexican club [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]]. He finished the pre-season campaign appearing in seven of the eight pre-season matches Real Madrid contested.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

Varane made his competitive debut for Real Madrid on 21 September in the team's league match against [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]]. He started the match at centre-back alongside [[Ricardo Carvalho]] as the match ended 0–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2011/9/21/2440810/real-madrid-at-racing-santander-recap-madrid-cant-score |title=Real Madrid at Racing Santander Recap: Madrid Can't Score |date=21 September 2011 |work=managingmadrid.com}}</ref> In the team's next league match three days later against [[Rayo Vallecano]], Varane started and scored his first goal for the club after a flying back-heel shot following a [[Mesut Özil]] corner. Real Madrid won the match 6–2. Varane's goal made him the youngest foreign player at 18 years and 152 days to score a goal in a competitive match for Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tv5.org/cms/chaine-francophone/Sports/football/p-15281-Real-Varane-entre-deja-dans-l-histoire.htm?item_id=7947 |title=Real: Varane entre déjà dans l'histoire |date=14 August 2011 |work=[[TV5 Monde]]|access-date=25 September 2011 |language=fr}}</ref> On 27 September, he made his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut in a 3–0 group stage win over Dutch club [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2007592--real-madrid-vs-ajax/ |publisher=UEFA |title=Masterful Madrid too much for Ajax |date=27 September 2011 |access-date=7 December 2011}}</ref> Two months later, Varane made his second Champions League appearance against Croatian club [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]]. In the match, Varane started and assisted on the team's fifth goal, scored by [[José Callejón]], in a 6–2 win. The victory ensured Real Madrid first place in its group.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2007639--real-madrid-vs-gnk-dinamo/ |publisher=UEFA |title=Perfect Madrid put six past Dinamo |date=22 November 2011 |access-date=7 December 2011}}</ref>

====2012–2016: First-team regular, UEFA Champions League wins====
Ahead of the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]], Varane switched to the number 2 shirt. After failing to appear in Real Madrid's first four league matches, he made his season debut on 18 September in the club's opening UEFA Champions League group stage match against English club [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. Varane started and played the entire match as Real Madrid won 3–2.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2009503--real-madrid-vs-man-city/ |publisher=UEFA |title=Ronaldo completes remarkable Madrid comeback |date=18 September 2012 |access-date=19 September 2012}}</ref>

On 30 January 2013, Varane made his ''[[El Clásico]]'' debut against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey]]. He stopped a group of dangerous attempts from Barcelona, including a shot from [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] that he cleared from the goal line. He capped his performance with a headed goal in the game, which ended 1–1. He also became the second-youngest foreign player to score for Real Madrid in a Clásico match. In the return leg at the [[Camp Nou]] on 26 February 2013, Varane scored Madrid's third goal in a 3–1 away win with a header from a corner kick by Mesut Özil. Varane gained praise from former World Cup winner [[Bixente Lizarazu]] after his performances against Barcelona and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. He said, "We are talking about a kid at Real Madrid who has unseated [[Pepe (footballer, born February 1983)|Pepe]], and Pepe, with all his stuff, is still a great centre-half. His performance against Manchester United and Barcelona was extraordinary". Varane continued to impress in the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] quarter final first leg against [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]], where he helped Madrid keep a clean sheet in a 3–0 triumph. All of his 27 passes found his teammates without any interception, and all of his tackles succeeded, with most on [[Didier Drogba]].{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

In April 2013, Varane was named by [[Marca (newspaper)|''Marca'']] readers as a member of the "Best foreign eleven in [[History of Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid's history]]".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.marca.com/2013/04/11/en/football/real_madrid/1365709938.html |title=The best foreign eleven in Real Madrid's history |date=12 April 2013 |work=Marca |location=Spain|access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref> On 14 May 2013, Varane successfully underwent an operation on his right knee after an injury he had picked up during his last 2012–13 league match against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/soccer-spain-varane-idINDEE94B08J20130512 |title=Real defender Varane to have surgery on knee injury |date=13 May 2013 |work=Reuters|access-date=16 July 2021}}</ref>

Varane came on as an injury-time substitute for [[Karim Benzema]] in the [[2014 Copa del Rey Final]] which Real Madrid won 2–1 against Barcelona on 16 April.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 April 2014 |title=Madrid crowned clasico kings |url=https://www.espnfc.com/us/en/report/391361/report.html?soccernet=true |url-status=dead |access-date=15 May 2014 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=20 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140420191953/http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/391361/report.html?soccernet=true }}</ref> He played all 120 minutes of Real Madrid's 4–1 win over [[Atlético Madrid]] in the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final]], in place of the more experienced Pepe. In added time at the end of extra time, after [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] scored the last goal, Varane kicked the ball towards Atlético manager [[Diego Simeone]], causing him to run onto the pitch in anger. Simeone was sent to the stands and Varane booked for the incident. After the game, Atlético captain [[Gabi (footballer, born 1983)|Gabi]] excused Varane due to his youth, while Simeone himself said, "I also made a mistake with my reaction. He's a young guy with a bright future."<ref>{{cite news |title=Simeone squares up to Varane |url=https://www.marca.com/2014/05/25/en/football/spanish_football/1400974294.html|access-date=25 May 2014 |newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=25 May 2014}}</ref> On 18 September 2014, Varane signed a new six-year contract to keep him at Real Madrid until 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/09/official-statement-varane |title=Official statement: Varane |date=18 September 2014|access-date=18 September 2014 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> He was a part-time squad player when the team won the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/ |title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again |date=28 May 2016 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

====2016–2021: Continued success====
[[File:FC RB Salzburg v.Real Madrid (Testspiel, 7. August 2019) 30.jpg|thumb|upright|Varane playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2019]]

Despite having a few injuries during the season, he made 23 appearances, when Madrid won the 2016–17 La Liga.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17 |title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17 |date=21 May 2017 |work=laliga.es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301 |title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory at Malaga |date=21 May 2017 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was starting in the [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] when Madrid won the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/ |title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff |date=3 June 2017 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

Varane's contract was extended until 2022 on 27 September 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/varanes-contract-extension |title=Ceremony to mark Raphaël Varane's contract renewal |date=27 September 2017 |publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> During the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]], he made eleven appearances, when Madrid won their 13th Champions League title and completed a hattrick of [[UEFA Champions League|UCL]] titles under [[Zinedine Zidane]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/ |title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick |date=26 May 2018 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref> Following his club and international performances throughout the year, he was included in the 30-man shortlist for the [[2018 Ballon d'Or]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Dobson |first=Mark |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/oct/08/soccer-ballon-dor-football-ronaldo-messi-kane-salah-kirby-bronze-hazard-liverpool-chelsea-real |title=Ballon d'Or 2018: contenders for football's global honour revealed |date=8 October 2018|access-date=1 September 2020 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> finishing in seventh place in the final ranking.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2018 |title=Le classement final du Ballon d'Or France Football 2018 |url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Le-classement-final-du-ballon-d-or-france-football-2018/964814 |work=France Football |language=fr}}</ref> He was also placed ninth in [[The Best FIFA Football Awards 2018|The Best FIFA Men's Player]] behind [[Kevin De Bruyne]],<ref name="Voting Results">{{cite web |date=24 September 2018 |title=FIFA Football Awards 2018 – Voting Results |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/10753307bf424cff/original/o1m6b5xups6mdzeq454o-pdf.pdf|access-date=24 September 2018 |publisher=FIFA}}</ref> and was elected as the starting centre-back for both the 2018 [[FIFPRO World 11|FIFPRO Men's World 11]]<ref>{{cite web |date=24 September 2018 |title=DE GEA, KANTE AND MBAPPE IN WORLD 11 |url=https://www.fifpro.org/news/de-gea-kante-mbappe-in-world-11/en/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180925025843/https://www.fifpro.org/news/de-gea-kante-mbappe-in-world-11/en/|archive-date=25 September 2018|access-date=13 December 2019 |publisher=Fédération Internationale des Associations de Footballeurs Professionnels}}</ref> and the [[UEFA Team of the Year#Team of the Year 2018|UEFA Team of the Year]].<ref name="team2018">{{cite web |date=11 January 2019 |title=UEFA.com fans' Team of the Year 2018 revealed |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d8202451389-96824880e336-1000--uefa-com-fans-team-of-the-year-2018-revealed/|access-date=11 January 2019 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

During the [[2018–19 Real Madrid CF season|2018–19 season]], he made 43 appearances, while winning the [[2018 FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/real-madrid-win-third-successive-global-crown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222230424/https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/real-madrid-win-third-successive-global-crown |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 December 2018 |title=Real Madrid win third successive global crown |publisher=FIFA |date=22 December 2018 |access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> He was a regular starter during the following league season, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]] title.<ref name="Liga">{{cite news |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html |title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season |date=17 July 2020 |access-date=17 July 2020 |newspaper=Marca |location=Spain}}</ref> During the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], Madrid were eliminated in the round of 16 by Manchester City.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 August 2020 |title=Manchester City 2–1 Real Madrid: Pep Guardiola's side win 4–2 on aggregate |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53683510 |access-date=8 August 2020}}</ref> In the second leg at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]], [[Manchester]], Madrid lost the game 2–1, with Varane being deemed to be at fault for both goals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirkland |first=Alex |date=7 August 2020 |title=Varane 4/10 as defensive mistakes doom Madrid to Champions League exit |url=https://global.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37585892 |access-date=15 June 2025 |website=ESPN}}</ref> He would later issue an apology for his mistakes.<ref>{{Cite web |title='This is my defeat' – Varane takes responsibility for Madrid Champions League exit after Man City horror show |website=Goal |publisher=DAZN Group |location=Leeds |url=https://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/this-is-my-defeat-varane-takes-responsibility-for-madrid/14uydsujwwf5w1x8omjrzulri6 |date=7 August 2020 |access-date=8 August 2020}}</ref>

===Manchester United===
[[File:Manchester United v Newcastle United, 11 September 2021 (30).jpg|thumb|upright|Varane playing for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in 2021]]

On 27 July 2021, it was announced that [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and Real Madrid had reached an agreement for Varane's transfer, subject to a medical and to player terms being finalised.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Man Utd reaches agreement for Raphael Varane transfer from Real Madrid |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-reaches-agreement-for-raphael-varane-transfer-from-real-madrid|access-date=27 July 2021 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Official Announcement: Raphaël Varane |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/07/27/official-announcement-raphael-varane|access-date=27 July 2021 |website=realmadrid.com}}</ref> The transfer was completed on 14 August 2021, after Varane was announced in front of a packed [[Old Trafford]] crowd ahead of United's [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League]] opener against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=United announce Varane signing |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/raphael-varane-completes-transfer-from-real-madrid-to-manchester-united|access-date=14 August 2021 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Raphael Varane: Manchester United sign France defender on four-year deal |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58176187 |work=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2021 |access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref> He was given the number 19 shirt previously worn by [[Amad Diallo]], which he also donned during his first season with Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Varane squad number revealed |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/raphael-varane-squad-number-at-man-utd-revealed|access-date=14 August 2021 |date=14 August 2021 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |first=Matthew |last=Holt}}</ref> He made his debut on 29 August 2021 and contributed an assist to the winning goal in a 1–0 win away against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-1 Manchester United: Mason Greenwood hits winner |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58295875|access-date=29 August 2021 |date=29 August 2021 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |first=Neil |last=Johnston}}</ref> On 2 May 2022, Varane scored his first goal for the club in a 3–0 league win against [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stone |first=Simon |date=2 May 2022 |title=Man Utd 3-0 Brentford: Fernandes, Ronaldo & Varane score in morale-boosting win |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61212449 |access-date=3 May 2022}}</ref>

On 22 October 2022, Varane suffered a leg injury in a Premier League match against Chelsea. United manager [[Erik ten Hag]] said in a press conference on 26 October that the injury would rule Varane out of all of the club's matches ahead of the break for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], leaving his chances of being selected in the France squad for the tournament uncertain.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United: Raphael Varane out until World Cup, Cristiano Ronaldo back in squad for Europa League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63399744 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 October 2022 |access-date=27 October 2022}}</ref>

On 26 February 2023, Raphaël Varane won his first trophy with United as he took place in the starting line-up in the [[EFL Cup]] final against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[Wembley stadium|Wembley]], which Manchester United won 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Man Utd 2-0 Newcastle: Erik ten Hag's side win Carabao Cup to end six-year trophy drought |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11938/12817244/man-utd-2-0-newcastle-erik-ten-hags-side-win-carabao-cup-to-end-six-year-trophy-drought |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> On 14 August 2023, Varane scored the winning goal in Manchester United's first game of the [[2023–24 Premier League|2023–24 season]] in a 1–0 win against Wolverhampton Wanderers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/aug/14/manchester-united-wolves-premier-league-match-report |title=Raphaël Varane gives nervy Manchester United win against lively Wolves |work=The Guardian |date=14 August 2023 }}</ref>

On 14 May 2024, Varane announced that he would depart the club at the end of the season as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-14 |title=Varane announces departure from United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/raphael-varane-announces-departure-from-man-utd |access-date=2024-05-14 |publisher=Manchester United FC |language=en}}</ref> On 25 May 2024, Varane made his final appearance for the ''Red Devils'', lifting the [[FA Cup]] after a 2–1 [[2024 FA Cup final|victory]] against local rivals [[Manchester City]] at Wembley. In total, he made 95 appearances for United and scored two goals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/five-man-utd-players-leave-29234073.amp|publisher=Wales Online|title=Five Man Utd players to leave after FA Cup win|date=25 May 2024 }}</ref>

===Como and retirement===
On 28 July 2024, it was announced that [[Serie A]] club [[Como 1907|Como]] signed Varane on a two-year deal with an option to extend.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Como 1907 sign World Cup and four time Champions League winner Raphaël Varane|url=https://comofootball.com/en/como-1907-sign-raphael-varane/|date=28 July 2024 |access-date=28 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728193057/https://comofootball.com/en/como-1907-sign-raphael-varane/|website=comofootball.com |archive-date=28 July 2024|language=en|publisher=Como 1907|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 August, he sustained a knee injury in the first half of a [[2024–25 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] match against [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], his first match with the club.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lambourne |first=Jake |url=https://talksport.com/football/2005010/raphael-varane-como-debut-injury-serie-a/ |title=Raphael Varane's Como debut gets off to worst start possible after just 20 minutes in Cesc Fabregas' first match in charge |publisher=talkSPORT |date=13 August 2024 }}</ref> Later that month, he was excluded from the club's Serie A squad list.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.footitalia.com/varane-excluded-from-comos-serie-a-squad-list/ |title=Varane excluded from Como's Serie A squad list |publisher=FootItalia.com |date=31 August 2024 }}</ref> He announced his retirement on 25 September 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mogan |first=Tony |date=2024-09-25 |title=Ex-Man Utd star announces shock retirement after just 23 minutes for new club |url=https://metro.co.uk/2024/09/25/former-man-utd-star-announces-shock-retirement-just-23-minutes-new-club-21666985/ |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=Metro |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-25 |title=Raphael Varane: Former Manchester United, Real Madrid and France defender retires aged 31 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ced0yjn3wj0o |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-retirada-de-raphael-varane-25-09-2024|title=Official Announcement: Raphaël Varane has retired | date=25 September 2024|website=[[Real Madrid CF]]}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
[[File:Raphaël Varane (1).jpg|thumb|upright|Varane playing for [[France national under-21 football team|France U21]] in 2011]]

Varane was a [[France national youth football team|France youth international]] having earned caps at [[France national under-18 football team|under-18]], [[France national under-20 football team|under-20]] and [[France national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fff.fr/equipe-nationale/joueur/8493-varane-raphael/fiche.html |title=Raphaël Varane |publisher=French Football Federation|access-date=1 November 2021}}</ref>

Prior to playing for the under-18 team, he was called up to the under-17 team but did not make an appearance.<ref name="varane_career"/> Varane made his debut with the under-18 team on 24 August 2010 in a [[Friendly (association football)|friendly match]] against [[Denmark national under-18 football team|Denmark]]. On his debut, he scored the final goal in a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fff.fr/selections/m18ans/actualite/534518.shtml |publisher=French Football Federation |title=Des débuts victorieux (2–0) |language=fr |date=24 August 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011}}</ref> Varane turned down subsequent call-ups to the under-18 team because of his increased participation with the Lens first team and, as a result, missed the ''Tournoi de Limoges'' and a tournament in [[Israel]].<ref name="varane_antilles"/> On 3 February 2011, he was called up to the under-21 team by coach [[Erick Mombaerts]] for the first time for a friendly match against [[Slovakia national under-21 football team|Slovakia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fr.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1376567.html |publisher=[[FIFA|Fédération Internationale de Football Association]] |title=Kakuta et Varane avec les Espoirs |language=fr |date=3 February 2011 |access-date=18 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110210131738/http://fr.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1376567.html |archive-date=10 February 2011}}</ref> Varane described the call up as "a huge surprise".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fff.fr/selections/espoirs/actualite/536376.shtml |publisher=French Football Federation |title=Varane: "Une énorme surprise" |language=fr |date=8 February 2011 |access-date=18 May 2011}}</ref> He earned his first under-21 cap and start in the match against Slovakia playing the entire match in a 3–1 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fff.fr/servfff/fiche_joueur_new/match.php?id_match=1357 |publisher=French Football Federation |title=France 3–1 Slovaquie |language=fr |date=8 February 2011 |access-date=18 May 2011}}</ref> On 15 November, Varane scored his first under-21 goal in a 2–0 [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship qualification|2013 Euro U-21 qualifying]] win over Slovakia. The victory ensured France qualification to at least the competition's qualifying play-offs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/match/2006954--france-vs-slovakia/ |publisher=UEFA |title=France open up six-point lead with Slovakia win |date=15 November 2011 |access-date=7 December 2011}}</ref>

===Senior===
[[File:Raphael Varane - France v Armenia.jpg|thumb|upright|Varane playing for [[France national football team|France]] in 2014]]

In August 2012, Varane was called up to the France national team for a friendly against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]], but was an unused substitute.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://m.goal.com/s/en-india/news/3296321/ |title=Varane included in France squad for Uruguay friendly |date=9 August 2013 |work=goal.com|access-date=26 December 2014|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402203118/http://m.goal.com/s/en-india/news/3296321/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He started his first match for France on 22 March 2013 in a qualifier for the World Cup against [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]], a 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news |title=France breeze past Georgia |url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/253591/report|access-date=14 May 2014 |newspaper=[[Sky Sports News]] |date=22 March 2013}}</ref> On 13 May 2014, he was included in [[Didier Deschamps]]' squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=World Cup 2014: Samir Nasri and Gael Clichy not in France squad |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27401306|access-date=14 May 2014 |website=BBC Sport |date=13 May 2014}}</ref>

On 15 June 2014, he partnered [[Mamadou Sakho]] in central defence for ''Les Bleus''{{'}} first World Cup fixture—a 3–0 win over [[Honduras national football team|Honduras]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25285092 |title=France 3–0 Honduras |date=15 June 2014|access-date=16 June 2014 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was also in the starting line-up for the second group match against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and the [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout matches]] against [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]] and [[Germany national football team|Germany]], as France were eliminated at the quarter-final stage by the Germans 1–0.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jul/04/france-germany-world-cup-2014-quarter-final-match-report |first=David |last=Hytner |date=5 July 2014 |title=Germany reach World Cup semi-finals as Mats Hummels header sinks France |newspaper=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> Varane took the blame for allowing [[Mats Hummels]] to hold him off at the critical set-piece which allowed the German defender to head the winning goal.<ref name="FRAURU">{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/fifa-world-cup-2018/varane-exorcises-ghosts-of-brazil-as-france-look-to-semi-finals-20180708-p4zq6i.html |title=Varane exorcises ghosts of Brazil as France look to semi-finals |date=8 July 2018}}</ref>
In spite of this, Varane was named on the three-man shortlist for the tournament's [[2014 FIFA World Cup#Awards|Best Young Player]] award.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28274011 |title=World Cup 2014: Fifa announces Golden Ball shortlist |date=11 July 2014|access-date=12 July 2014 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 14 October, Varane became the youngest player to [[Captain (association football)|captain]] France when he took over from [[Blaise Matuidi]] at half time in a 3–0 win over [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/raphael-varane-becomes-frances-youngest-ever-captain-in-armenia-win/ |title=Raphael Varane became France's youngest ever captain in Armenia win|access-date=4 April 2015 |work=101 Great Goals|archive-date=9 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150409182102/http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/raphael-varane-becomes-frances-youngest-ever-captain-in-armenia-win/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was then selected as the team's starting captain for a home friendly against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] on 18 November, where he scored his first international goal to give ''Les Bleus'' a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |title=France 1–0 Sweden: Varane secures win for dominant Bleus |url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/france-vs-sweden/1946143/report|access-date=19 November 2014 |work=Goal.com |date=18 November 2014}}</ref>

On 24 May 2016, he was ruled out of [[UEFA Euro 2016]] with a thigh injury, and was replaced by [[Adil Rami]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36375392 |title=Euro 2016: Real Madrid defender Raphael Varane out of France squad |date=24 May 2016 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 17 May 2018, Varane was called up to France's [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|23-man squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12025/11376691/alexandre-lacazette-and-anthony-martial-on-standby-for-france-world-cup-squad-and-dimitri-payet-out |title=Alexandre Lacazette and Anthony Martial on standby for France World Cup squad and Dimitri Payet out – soccer News – Sky Sports |website=skysports.com}}</ref> He would go on to start in all seven of France's games and play every minute. In the quarter-final against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]], Varane scored the opening goal with a header in France's 2–0 victory.<ref name="FRAURU"/><ref>{{cite web |last=Bevan |first=Chris |title=Uruguay 0 France 2 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44652179 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=6 July 2018 |location=Nizhny Novgorod |date=6 July 2018}}</ref> France later went on to win the competition for the second time in history, and Varane became only the fourth player to be a World Cup champion and Champions League winner in the same year, after [[Christian Karembeu]] (in 1998), [[Roberto Carlos]] (in 2002) and [[Sami Khedira]] (in 2014). All the players, like Varane, were playing for Real Madrid at the time they won the World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=16 July 2018 |language=fr |title=Raphaël Varane est le quatrième joueur à remporter la Ligue des champions et la Coupe du monde la même saison |url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Raphael-varane-est-le-quatrieme-joueur-a-remporter-la-ligue-des-champions-et-la-coupe-du-monde-la-meme-saison/923122 |publisher=[[France Football]]}}</ref>

In May 2021, he was included in the squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Orsini |first=Vincent |url=https://www.fff.fr/article/2859-la-liste-des-vingt-six-pour-l-uefa-euro-2020.html |title=La liste des vingt-six pour l'UEFA Euro 2020 |trans-title=The list of 26 for UEFA Euro 2020 |work=French Football Federation |date=18 May 2021 |access-date=18 May 2021 |language=fr}}</ref> He played in every minute of France's four matches at the tournament, including the period of extra time at the end of their round of 16 match against Switzerland; that match went to penalties, but Varane was not selected to take one of the first five kicks as France lost 5–4.{{citation needed|date=October 2022}}

In November 2022, Varane made the 26-man squad for France for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-11-16 |title=FIFA World Cup 2022 {{!}} Full France squad and schedule |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sport/football/fifa-world-cup-2022-full-france-squad-and-schedule/article66105297.ece |access-date=2023-03-01 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> On 18 December, Varane was named in the starting line-up for France as they played their second successive World Cup final, eventually losing 4–2 on penalties to [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |date=2022-12-18 |title=Argentina beat France on penalties to win World Cup after stunning final |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/dec/18/world-cup-final-argentina-france-match-report |access-date=2023-03-01 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

On 2 February 2023, at 29 years old, Varane announced his retirement from international football via his [[Instagram]] account. The defender shared a series of photos from his international career alongside the announcement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raphael Varane on Instagram: "Représenter notre magnifique pays pendant une décennie a été l'un des plus grands honneurs de ma vie. A chaque fois que j'ai porté ce maillot bleu si spécial, j'ai ressenti une immense fierté. Le devoir de tout donner, de jouer avec mon cœur et de gagner à chaque fois qu'on entrait sur le terrain. Cela fait plusieurs mois que j'y réfléchis et j'ai décidé que c'était le bon moment pour moi de prendre ma retraite internationale. Enfant, je me rappelle avoir suivi France 98, cette équipe, ces joueurs qui nous ont fait vivre des émotions indescriptibles. Je rêvais de faire comme nos héros et, 20 ans après, j'ai vécu l'une des plus belles expériences de ma vie, de celles qui m'ont rendu vraiment fier. On a ramené la Coupe à la maison !! Je ne l'oublierai jamais. Je ressens toujours chacune des émotions ressenties ce jour-là, le 15 juillet 2018. Ça a été l'un des moments les plus formidables et les plus mémorables de ma vie. Cette victoire que nous avons remportée tous ensemble n'aurait jamais été possible sans le soutien de Didier Deschamps, de chacun des membres de l'encadrement et de notre staff durant ces années, de mes coéquipiers qui ont défendu notre maillot à chacun de nos matchs. Mais plus important encore, cette victoire n'aurait pas été possible sans le soutien de chacun d'entre vous tout au long de ce chemin. Votre ferveur, les célébrations et les souvenirs de notre retour en France resteront gravés à jamais en moi. Même après la défaite en finale l'année dernière, avec certes un beau parcours, vous nous avez accueillis en héros à notre retour. A chacune et à chacun de vous, mille fois MERCI ! Ces moments avec vous me manqueront c'est certain, mais le moment est venu pour la nouvelle génération de prendre le relais. Nous avons un groupe de jeunes joueurs talentueux qui est prêt à prendre la relève, qui mérite d'avoir sa chance et qui a besoin de vous. Du plus profond de mon cœur, merci. Rapha. 💙🤍♥️" |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CoKMpXSOZtt/ |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=Instagram |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=France's Varane retires from international football |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64498739 |access-date=2023-02-02}}</ref> The announcement marked the end of his ten-year run with the national team where he made 93 appearances and scored 5 goals.

== After football retirement ==
Having been a part of Como's team until 2024, after retirement, Varane took up a role on the Education board of the team partnering with [[Osian Roberts]] and Juliette Bolon by focusing on youth development and educating programs.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://comofootball.com/en/raphael-varane-from-world-cup-winner-to-the-board-of-education-at-como-1907/ | website=comofootball.com| title= Raphaël Varane: From World Cup Winner to the Board of Education at Como 1907| access-date = 27 August 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play ==
Varane was described by Lens youth coach [[Éric Assadourian]] as a "truly first-class player" who was "comfortable on both the tactical and technical level."<ref name="lensois">{{cite web |url=http://www.lensois.com/article-1909-qui-sont-varane-kondogbia-hazard-et-deligny.html |publisher=Lensois |title=Qui sont Varane, Kondogbia, Hazard et Deligny |language=fr |date=9 March 2010 |access-date=14 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713201142/http://www.lensois.com/article-1909-qui-sont-varane-kondogbia-hazard-et-deligny.html |archive-date=13 July 2011}}</ref> On 30 January 2013, the then-Real Madrid assistant coach [[Aitor Karanka]] talked about Varane in the press conference post-''[[El Clásico]]'' of the [[Copa del Rey]], saying, "It's obvious that Varane has a good head on his shoulders and will keep improving."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/41828/karanka-the-team-did-an-amazing-job/ |title=Karanka: The team did an amazing job and really were good|access-date=30 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322010738/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/41828/karanka-the-team-did-an-amazing-job/|archive-date=22 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Varane's height made him effective in the air, while his confidence on the ball allowed him to evade the opposing team's press and start attacking plays from the back with his passing.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2016/12/28/58642fda468aebaa7b8b458e.html |title=Ramos and Varane to be Real Madrid's defensive guardians in 2017 |newspaper=Marca |last=Jiménez |first=Rubén |language=en |date=28 December 2016 |access-date=24 June 2024 }}</ref>

Former France defender [[Frank Leboeuf]] believed that Varane had the potential to be better than Real Madrid legend [[Fernando Hierro]], saying to reporters, "Many compare him to Hierro due to his technique, but on the physical level he is stronger and he is much faster."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2013/03/27/3857599/lebouef-varane-could-surpass-hierro |title=Lebouef: Varane could surpass Hierro |website=Goal.com |access-date=27 February 2013}}</ref> Both Hierro and [[José Mourinho]] labelled Varane as one of the best defenders in world football.<ref name="goal1">{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2014/03/06/4665852/varane-best-defender-in-the-world-says-mourinho |title=Varane best defender in the world, says Mourinho |website=Goal.com}}</ref><ref name="goal2">{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spanish-football/2013/10/17/4339741/hierro-varane-is-the-worlds-best-defender |title=Hierro: Varane is the world's best defender |website=Goal.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Varane is married to his long-time partner Camille Tytgat,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/real-madrid-defender-raphael-varane-got-married-to-camille-tytgat-pictures-video/ |title=Real Madrid defender Raphaël Varane got married to Camille Tytgat [Pictures & Video]|access-date=21 June 2016 |publisher=101greatgoals.com|archive-date=11 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711062221/http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/real-madrid-defender-raphael-varane-got-married-to-camille-tytgat-pictures-video/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and they have a son named Ruben<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.realtotal.de/pepe-varane-franzose-erstmals-vater/ |title=Papa Varane: Franzose erstmals Vater|access-date=17 March 2018 |publisher=realtotal.de}}</ref> and a daughter named Anaïs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raphaël Varane, papa d'Anaïs |url=https://www.journaldesfemmes.fr/maman/bebe/1317400-people-prenoms-enfants-de-stars/2670415-raphael-varane-et-son-epouse|access-date=1 January 2021 |website=journaldesfemmes.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

When [[Zinedine Zidane]] called Varane about Real Madrid's interest in signing him in June 2011, Varane asked Zidane to call him back because he was in the middle of studying for his baccalaureate exam.<ref>{{cite news |last=Holyman |first=Ian |date=12 November 2014 |title=Raphael Varane made Zidane call him back about Real Madrid move |url=https://www.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37390347 |access-date=15 June 2025 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

His half-brother, [[Jonathan Varane]], is a professional footballer who plays for [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/2024/august/04/qpr-complete-signing-of-jonathan-varane/|title=Official website of Queens Park Rangers for the latest news from Loftus Road|first=QPR|last=FC|website=QPR FC}}</ref> His sister, Annabelle Varane, was Miss Nord-Pas-de-Calais 2018 and competed in [[Miss France 2019]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Miss France Annabelle Varane, la sœur de Raphaël, élue Miss Nord-Pas-de-Calais |date=13 October 2018 |url=http://lavdn.lavoixdunord.fr/468818/article/2018-10-13/election-de-miss-nord-pas-de-calais-suivez-la-soiree-en-direct}}</ref>

In an interview for ''[[L'Équipe]]'' in April 2024, Varane said that [[Concussions in sport#Association football|concussions]] suffered in various official matches throughout his career had "damaged [his] body", as he suggested to avoid teaching children heading and called for wider awareness among players around the dangers of repeated head trauma to brain health.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marcelin |first=Vincent |date=2 April 2024 |title=Raphaël Varane : " J'ai abîmé mon corps " |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Article/Raphael-varane-j-ai-abime-mon-corps/1458158 |url-access=subscription |access-date=3 April 2024 |website=[[L'Équipe]] |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Millar |first=Colin |date=2 April 2024 |title=Varane opens up on 'damage' from football concussions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5385097/2024/04/02/raphael-varane-man-united-concussion/ |url-access=registration |access-date=3 April 2024 |website=[[The Athletic]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2 April 2024 |title='I've damaged my body': Raphaël Varane warns against trauma of concussions |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/apr/02/raphael-varane-manchester-united-concussion-football |access-date=3 April 2024 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He also revealed how symptoms of concussions had a negative impact on some of his performances, including the [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#France vs Germany|quarter-final match]] against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] and the second leg of the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16 match]] against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League]].<ref name=":0"/><ref name=":1"/>

==Honours==
